text:
alex-cs: Customer (AcmeX) reports SSE stream dropping after ~125s. Client reconnects and ends up double-charging because resumed stream triggers new token usage. They attached a curl repro and some backend logs. Can we triage?

alex-cs: curl they used:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-stream" -o -
# client prints events for ~30s then silent, then reconnects
```
ingrid-sre: Do we have request ids / stream ids? 125s is odd — ALB default idle is 60s, Cloudflare 100s. :eyes: Could be CF or our nginx buffering/timeout.
alex-cs: They sent ALB config + screenshot: Cloudflare in front of ALB -> Nginx -> app. Request ids: req=abcd-1234 stream_id=stream-9876. Backend log shows `write: broken pipe` at t=125s.
zach-eng: `write: broken pipe` usually means the downstream closed. If CF closes at 100s, backend keeps writing and gets broken pipe later. Need to reproduce bypassing CF and ALB. Will try direct NLB.
eli-ops: FYI Cloudflare has a ~100s idle TCP timeout for some plans. If we have silence longer than that CF may close. Our SSE path does not send periodic heartbeats by default. Workaround: send a small SSE comment/whitespace every 20-30s to keep connection active. :thinking:
ingrid-sre: Can we get a repro plan for eng? Steps: 1) curl direct to NLB to bypass CF/ALB 2) reproduce with rate-limited server so outbound stalls 3) tcpdump on edge and backend 4) collect ALB logs. @zach-eng can you run?
zach-eng: Yep. I'll run the 4-step repro. Quick mitigations to suggest to customer: set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300;` on nginx, and increase ALB idle timeout to 300. Also advise Cloudflare to increase origin timeout or use a Worker to forward heartbeat.
alex-cs: Customer also saw auth failures when reconnecting — token rotation race: client refreshes token between connections and resume attempt uses old session id causing 401 then a new generation that billed again.
eli-ops: That's important — billing duplication looks like race between resume session and token refresh. Short-term: if reconnect uses a different auth token, treat it as a fresh session but ensure we don't double-credit previous partial output. Long-term: server should validate `session-id` vs auth-sub.
ingrid-sre: Created RLW-2043 to track "resume auth mismatch -> billing duplication". Priority: P1 for billing impact. Zach, can you add an immediate server-side guard to compare auth sub against stored session owner and refuse resume if mismatched?
zach-eng: Will do. Also ran tests: direct NLB -> backend stable at 5m, with Cloudflare in front it drops at ~102s consistently. So CF is the proximate cause. Repro logs attached in the ticket.
eli-ops: For customer-facing mitigation, recommend: 1) Bypass Cloudflare (test direct) 2) If CF required, enable a Worker to inject SSE comment heartbeats `: keepalive

` every 25s, or adjust Cloudflare origin timeout if possible. 3) Increase ALB idle timeout and disable proxy buffering on nginx.
alex-cs: Customer is ok to apply heartbeat workaround and change ALB/nginx configs. They asked for a one-pager with exact steps and a refund template for the duplicated billing.
eli-ops: I'll open a billing review and start the refund process, marking as P1 until we confirm patch + customer mitigation.
rb-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 - SSE disconnects via Cloudflare keepalive. Linked ticket RLW-2043.
alex-cs: I'll send the workaround steps and keep the customer in the loop. Thanks everyone.
